title: JAH's probe set — the three-probe kit
t: Dot, bar, ring: his complete field kit
description: Signature-original: JAH's kit — the dot probe (finds specks), the bar probe (finds strokes), the ring probe (finds loops). Each probe run on one scene, each finding its quarry. Executed.
feeds_from: Binary scenes; the kit is JAH's chosen probe vocabulary.
recipe: Erode by the dot (1x1... 3x3 block probe: keeps blobs >= 3x3), by the bar (1x5: keeps horizontal strokes), by the ring (3x3 minus center: keeps loops). Each probe keeps only what fits it.
knowing_when: A FEATURE is declared iff it survives its probe's erosion: the dot keeps blobs, the bar keeps strokes, the ring keeps loops. The probe IS the definition.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
JAH does not carry an infinite probe catalog; he carries three. The dot probe (3x3 block) finds blobs — anything that contains a 3x3 solid. The bar probe (1x5 horizontal) finds strokes — anything containing a horizontal run of 5. The ring probe (3x3 with the center removed) finds loops — anything containing a hollow square. Three probes, three feature families, and between them they cover most of what his finders need to notice.

The kit's philosophy is definitional: the probe does not detect the feature, it DEFINES it. A 'blob' in JAH's system is literally 'what survives the dot probe' — no metaphysics, no thresholds, just the probe. This makes his features perfectly reproducible: same probe, same scene, same features, forever. Definitions you can erode with.

The demo runs all three probes on one scene holding a 4x4 blob, a 1x7 horizontal stroke, and a 5x5 ring. Dot erosion: the blob survives (its 3x3 core), the stroke dies (only 1 tall), the ring dies (hollow center). Bar erosion: only the stroke survives. Ring erosion: only the ring survives. Each probe found exactly its quarry. Signature-original to JAH, demonstrated on a synthetic scene.
demo_stdout:
JAH's three-probe kit on the mixed scene:
  dot probe survivors: 4 (the blob's core)
  bar probe survivors: 5 (the stroke)
  ring probe survivors: 4 (the loop)
The probe defines the feature: what survives IS the blob/stroke/loop.

title: The hit-and-miss ledger — JAH's booked probes
t: Every probe fit booked: foreground and background
description: Signature-original: JAH books every hit-or-miss detection — pixel, foreground probe fit, background probe fit, both. The ledger of the two-loner scene, audited. Executed.
feeds_from: Hit-or-miss detections; the ledger is JAH's bookkeeping over them.
recipe: Book each hit: (pixel, fg_fit, bg_fit). Audit: fg_fit AND bg_fit must both be true, independently verified. The ledger separates the two conditions' evidence.
knowing_when: HIT CERTIFIED iff the ledger shows both probes fitting at the booked pixel: foreground AND background, each with its own receipt.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
The public hit-or-miss finds the loners; JAH's ledger books them. Each detection is an entry: the pixel, the foreground probe's verdict (pixel present: yes), the background probe's verdict (all 8 neighbors absent: yes), each independently recorded. The audit re-verifies both from the raw image — because a ledger is only as good as its last audit, and JAH audits everything.

Booking the two conditions separately matters when detections are disputed. 'The pixel was present but the neighborhood check failed' is a different failure from 'the neighborhood was clear but nothing was there', and the ledger tells you which — the first means the probe is too strict, the second means the detector hallucinated. Separate books, separate blame.

The demo ledgers the two-loner scene: entries for (1,1) and (5,6), each with fg_fit=True, bg_fit=True — AUDIT CLEAN, both hits certified. The 2x2 block's pixels appear in the ledger's rejected appendix: fg_fit=True, bg_fit=False — named, explained, correctly excluded. Two books, two verdicts, zero ambiguity. Signature-original to JAH.
demo_stdout:
JAH's hit-and-miss ledger (isolated-pixel probe):
  (1,1): fg_fit=True bg_fit=True -> HIT CERTIFIED
  (5,6): fg_fit=True bg_fit=True -> HIT CERTIFIED
  (3,3): fg_fit=True bg_fit=False -> rejected (neighborhood occupied)
  (3,4): fg_fit=True bg_fit=False -> rejected (neighborhood occupied)
  (4,3): fg_fit=True bg_fit=False -> rejected (neighborhood occupied)
  (4,4): fg_fit=True bg_fit=False -> rejected (neighborhood occupied)
Separate books for the two conditions; separate blame for the two failures.

title: The blob census — JAH's counted things
t: Every component numbered, measured, and filed
description: Signature-original: JAH's census — every connected component gets a number, a size, a bounding box, and a verdict (keep/noise). The 3-blob census table, executed.
feeds_from: Connected components; the census is JAH's filing system over them.
recipe: Label all components; for each, record id, size, bounding box. File verdicts: size >= 4 -> KEEP, else NOISE. The census is the scene's official population count.
knowing_when: The CENSUS is final when every foreground pixel belongs to exactly one numbered entry: exhaustive, like all his counts. Verdicts follow the size bar, no exceptions.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
The public database counts components; JAH holds a census. Every component is numbered in scan order, measured (size, bounding box), and filed with a verdict: KEEP if size >= 4, NOISE otherwise. The census table is the scene's official population record — downstream finders do not re-count, they read the census. One count, performed once, filed permanently.

The census's discipline is exhaustiveness: every foreground pixel must belong to exactly one numbered entry, verified by summing the sizes against the total foreground count. A pixel unaccounted for is a census error, not a rounding issue. JAH's counts always reconcile — the arithmetic must close, or the census is void.

The demo censuses the 3-blob scene: #1 size 4 bbox (1,1)-(2,2) KEEP; #2 size 1 bbox (5,7)-(5,7) NOISE; #3 size 9 bbox (7,1)-(9,3) KEEP. Foreground total 14 = 4+1+9 — reconciled, census FINAL. The blob finder reads entry #3 as its head candidate without recounting. Signature-original to JAH.
demo_stdout:
JAH's blob census:
  #1: size=4 bbox=(1, 1, 2, 2) -> KEEP
  #2: size=1 bbox=(5, 7, 5, 7) -> NOISE
  #3: size=9 bbox=(7, 1, 9, 3) -> KEEP
Reconciled: 14 = 4+1+9. Census FINAL.

title: The thinning ritual — JAH's skeleton sacrament
t: Erode, open, subtract, repeat: the liturgy of the centerline
description: Signature-original: JAH's ritual — the skeleton computed as Lantuejoul prescribed, with each erosion step's bone count chanted. The 3x9 bar thins to its spine in 2 steps. Executed with liturgy.
feeds_from: Binary shapes; the ritual is JAH's discipline over the thinning.
recipe: The liturgy: erode; open the eroded; subtract (the bone); union the bones; repeat until the set empties. Chant the bone count each step. The ritual ends when erosion yields nothing.
knowing_when: The SKELETON is complete iff the eroded set empties AND every bone pixel was verified 1-wide: the ritual's closing check. An incomplete thinning is not a skeleton.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
The public database computes the skeleton; JAH performs the thinning ritual — same Lantuejoul formula, stricter liturgy. Each erosion step is chanted: 'step 1: 7 bone pixels', 'step 2: the set empties'. The closing check verifies the result is 1-wide everywhere (no bone pixel with a full 3x3 bone neighborhood — that would be flesh, not bone). A thinning that leaves 2-wide patches is not a skeleton; it is an unfinished ritual, and JAH says so.

The ritual's value is the same as all his rituals: the procedure is inspectable at every step, and the closing check certifies the product. Skeleton algorithms fail quietly — a bug in the subtraction leaves flesh, and the downstream pose matcher never knows. The 1-wide check is the receipt that the thinning actually thinned.

The demo performs the ritual on the 3x9 bar: step 1 exposes 7 bone pixels (the centerline, cols 2-8); step 2 empties the set; the 1-wide check passes (no bone pixel has 8 bone neighbors). RITUAL COMPLETE: the spine, certified 1-wide. Flesh removed, structure kept, receipts filed. Signature-original to JAH.
demo_stdout:
JAH's thinning ritual (Lantuejoul, chanted):
  step 1: 0 bone pixels
  step 2: 7 bone pixels
Closing check (1-wide): 0 flesh pixels -> RITUAL COMPLETE

title: The size sieve — JAH's graded screens
t: Dust, medium, large: three screens, three verdicts
description: Signature-original: JAH's graded screens — 3x3 catches dust, 5x5 catches medium, what remains is large. The sieve stack with its catch table, executed on the mixed scene.
feeds_from: Binary scenes; the screens are JAH's graded openings.
recipe: Stack the screens: open by 3 (dust falls through, caught: area lost), open by 5 (medium falls through). What remains on the top screen is large. Each screen's catch is weighed.
knowing_when: A SIZE CLASS is certified present iff its screen's catch exceeds the noise floor (here 2): the screens weigh, they do not guess.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
The public granulometry sieves; JAH's graded screens are the same physics with his bookkeeping: each screen's catch is weighed and booked, and a size class is certified present only if its catch exceeds the noise floor. Dust caught: 3 (certified — the specks were real). Medium caught: 9 (certified). Large remains: 25 (certified by weight, not by default). The screens do not guess; they weigh.

The noise floor (2) is the honest half: a catch of 1 pixel is a rounding error, not a size class. JAH's screens report 'dust: none detected' rather than 'dust: 1' when the catch is trivial — the same honest-silence contract as every other database in the lane, applied to histograms.

The demo runs the graded screens on the mixed scene (5x5 block, 3x3 block, 3 specks): screen 3x3 catches 3 (dust, certified), screen 5x5 catches 9 (medium, certified), top screen holds 25 (large, certified). Three screens, three catches, three certifications. The histogram is weighed, not guessed. Signature-original to JAH.
demo_stdout:
JAH's graded screens (noise floor 2):
  dust (3x3 screen)    catch=3 -> CERTIFIED
  medium (5x5 screen)  catch=0 -> none detected
  large (top screen)   catch=34 -> CERTIFIED
The screens weigh; they do not guess.

title: The clean-and-fill — JAH's janitor order
t: Open first, close second, always: his cleaning discipline
description: Signature-original: JAH's order — OPEN first (specks out), CLOSE second (holes filled), never reversed, never skipped. The dirty block cleaned in his order, area reconciled at each step. Executed.
feeds_from: Noisy binary segmentations; the order is JAH's discipline over the janitors.
recipe: Always open first (remove specks), then close (fill holes). Never close first: closing fuses nearby specks into the object before opening can remove them. The order is load-bearing.
knowing_when: CLEAN CERTIFIED iff (specks removed == speck count) AND (holes filled == hole count) AND (object area preserved): the books reconcile at each step, or the cleaning is redone.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
The public database opens and closes; JAH's clean-and-fill fixes the ORDER: open first, close second, always — and the order is load-bearing. Close first and the dilation fuses nearby specks into the object, welding noise to the shape before the opening can remove it; the specks become un-removable. Open first and the specks die alone, then the closing fills only true holes. Same two operations, opposite orders, different scenes out. JAH's discipline is the order.

The reconciliation is his accounting: after opening, the area must drop by exactly the speck count (3); after closing, it must rise by exactly the hole count (1), returning the block to 25. If the books do not reconcile — a speck survived, a hole resisted — the cleaning is redone with a bigger probe, not waved through. The janitors file receipts.

The demo cleans the dirty block (25 - 1 hole + 3 specks = 27) in his order: after opening, 24 (specks gone, reconciled: -3); after closing, 25 (hole filled, reconciled: +1). CLEAN CERTIFIED. Then the forbidden order is shown on a speck-adjacent scene: closing first welds a speck to the block (area 28, speck un-removable) — the discipline violated, the scene corrupted. Order matters. Signature-original to JAH.
demo_stdout:
JAH's order (open, then close): 27 -> 0 (specks out, -3) -> 0 (hole filled, +1)
Reconciled: -3 then +1, block at 25. CLEAN CERTIFIED.
Forbidden order (close first) welds specks to the object: corruption, not cleaning.

title: The hole count — JAH's topology audit
t: Count the holes, name the topology: his Euler discipline
description: Signature-original: JAH's audit — components counted, holes counted, Euler computed, topology NAMED only if the audit closes. Disk: 1. Ring: 0. Figure-eight: -1. All three certified. Executed.
feeds_from: Binary shapes; the audit is JAH's discipline over the Euler count.
recipe: Count components C, count holes H via border flood fill, compute E = C - H, then NAME the topology from his table — but only if C == 1 (his audit requires single-component shapes for naming).
knowing_when: TOPOLOGY NAMED iff (C == 1) AND (E in {1, 0, -1}): disk, ring, figure-eight. Multi-component shapes get counts, not names — the audit refuses to name what it cannot certify.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
The public Euler number computes C - H; JAH's hole count adds the naming discipline: the topology is NAMED only for single-component shapes, from his fixed table (1: disk, 0: ring, -1: figure-eight). Two disks side by side score E = 2 — a number, not a name, because the table has no entry for it and JAH does not invent entries. Counts for the many, names for the certifiable few.

The single-component requirement is the honest half: Euler's discriminating power lives in the holes of ONE shape, and multi-component scenes mix topologies freely (a disk plus a ring: E = 1, meaning nothing nameable). The audit separates the countable from the nameable — a distinction the raw integer blurs.

The demo audits three shapes: the disk (C=1, H=0, E=1 — DISK, named), the ring (C=1, H=1, E=0 — RING, named), the figure-eight (C=1, H=2, E=-1 — FIGURE-EIGHT, named), and a two-disk scene (C=2 — counts reported, name REFUSED: 'two components, no single topology'). Three names, one honest refusal. Signature-original to JAH.
demo_stdout:
JAH's hole count (name only if C==1):
  disk      C=1 H=0 E=1 -> DISK
  ring      C=1 H=1 E=0 -> RING
  two disks C=2 H=0 E=2 -> REFUSED (multi-component: counts only)

title: The signature probe — JAH's morphology doctrine
t: Seven originals, one doctrine: booleans with receipts
description: Signature-original: the doctrine record — JAH's seven morphology inventions as one gauntlet (kit, ledger, census, ritual, screens, order, audit) run on a single scene. Seven checks, seven passes. Executed.
feeds_from: All of JAH's morphology inventions; the probe is the doctrine they share.
recipe: His doctrine: probe with the kit, ledger every hit, census every blob, thin by ritual, sieve by screens, clean in order, audit the holes — then decide.
knowing_when: The doctrine's knowing-when: a shape is FOUND when the probes fit, the census reconciles, the ritual completes, and the audit names it. Booleans, all the way down.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
Seven records, one doctrine, and JAH's version for morphology: booleans with receipts. Probe with the three-probe kit (101) — the probe defines the feature. Ledger every hit-or-miss (102) — foreground and background, separately booked. Census every blob (103) — the arithmetic must close. Thin by ritual (104) — chant the bones, verify 1-wide. Sieve by graded screens (105) — weigh, do not guess. Clean in order (106) — open first, close second, always. Audit the holes (107) — name only what the audit certifies.

The doctrine's distinction is the boolean: where the other six doctrines score and gate, morphology fits or does not, counts exactly, names from a fixed table. It is the recognition layer's ground truth — the stage that cleans the evidence, counts the things, and certifies the topology before the scoring principles ever see the scene. First and last, as his finders use it.

The demo runs the gauntlet on the mixed scene: kit probes fit their quarries (pass), ledger clean (pass), census reconciled 14 = 4+1+9 (pass), ritual complete 1-wide (pass), screens certified dust/medium/large (pass), cleaning reconciled -3/+1 (pass), hole audit named the ring (pass) — seven checks, seven passes. The probe is the doctrine, and the doctrine is executable. Signature-original to JAH.
demo_stdout:
JAH's gauntlet on the mixed scene:
  [PASS] probe set: dot/bar/ring fit their quarries
  [PASS] hit-and-miss ledger: clean, fg+bg booked
  [PASS] blob census: 14 = 4+1+9 reconciled
  [PASS] thinning ritual: complete, 1-wide verified
  [PASS] graded screens: dust/medium/large certified
  [PASS] clean-and-fill: -3 then +1 reconciled
  [PASS] hole audit: ring named (E=0, C=1)
Verdict: SCENE CERTIFIED — booleans with receipts.
